items.titleEn: Minakuchi: Castle Town of Three Streets
items.bodyEn: Inside Minakuchi the Tōkaidō split into three parallel streets, a layout still visible today. In 1634 the shōgun Tokugawa Iemitsu built Minakuchi Castle here as a lodging for his journey to Kyoto; from 1682 it became the seat of the Minakuchi domain. Hiroshige's print skips the castle and shows the town's real fame: women shaving gourds into strips of kanpyō.
items.sourceNote: Hiroshige, Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833), 'Minakuchi: Meibutsu kanpyō'; 近江輿地志略 (1734)

items.titleEn: Kanpyō: A Gourd, Shaved and Dried
items.bodyEn: 干瓢 is literally 'dried gourd': 干, to dry, and 瓢, the gourd. The flesh of the bottle gourd 夕顔 is pared into a long ribbon and sun-dried. Alone 瓢 is read ヒョウ; after ん it hardens to ぴょう, as in 乾杯. When Minakuchi's lord moved to Shimotsuke in 1712 the craft went with him, which is why Tochigi leads today.
items.sourceNote: Kōjien (Iwanami), entry 干瓢; Hiroshige, 'Minakuchi: Meibutsu kanpyō' (c. 1833)

items.titleEn: 至: The Arrow Hits the Ground
items.bodyEn: The 至 of 〜に至る, 'to reach', shows something arriving. The Shuowen Jiezi read it as a bird swooping down to land; modern scholars, reading the oracle-bone form, see an arrow, point down, striking the ground, the line at the bottom. The idea is reaching the mark: 至急, utmost haste; 冬至, the winter solstice, where the sun reaches its limit.
items.sourceNote: Shuowen Jiezi (説文解字), entry 至: 鳥飛从高下至地也; Kanjigen (Gakken)

items.titleEn: まる Happens, める Makes It Happen
items.bodyEn: Several verb pairs at this station follow one tidy rule. From an adjective stem, 〜まる gives the intransitive change and 〜める the transitive one: 広まる spreads, 広める spreads it; 深まる deepens, 深める deepens it; likewise 高まる/高める and 強まる/強める. Remember the particles: 理解が深まる, but 理解を深める. Not every 〜まる verb has an adjective behind it (止まる, 始まる), but the pairing holds.
